scope: Narrow resource-lifetime review around schema loading and schema editor storage. This is not a whole-Eclipse handle audit.

historical_bug.title: Windows File Locks are obtained on bundles exporting extension points and not released.
historical_bug.bug_page_direct_access: Unavailable through the web retrieval tool in this session.
historical_bug.interpretation: An official historical schema/extension-point file-lock defect and its maintenance-release fix are documented. This does not identify the incident remembered by the user or prove a current recurrence.

resource_paths.finding: The input stream is scoped by try-with-resources. A JarURLConnection additionally has its JarFile closed in finally, including malformed-XML/model failures handled inside load(InputStream).
JarURLConnection caching is disabled. The API comment explicitly assigns a separate JarFile.close obligation and names Bug 326263.
The stream uses try-with-resources and the JarFile has a separate finally close; used by schema documentation and content-assist readers.
SchemaRegistry schema-URL lookup uses this helper; it opens ZipFile in try-with-resources even on an early return.
The editor-opening owner wraps ZipFile in try-with-resources. No whole-editor lifecycle execution was performed.
The IStorage implementation returns an entry stream from a caller-owned ZipFile. It does not open a second archive; ownership is with the creator, not each entry stream.
Calls StorageSchemaDescriptor for IStorageEditorInput, so the double-getContents fix belongs to an editor-storage path. No startup reachability was established.
Its URI-input fallback closes the EFS stream with try-with-resources. The superclass IStorage path was not independently exercised.
The adjacent manifest helper closes the stream and archive in separate try/catch blocks so one IOException does not skip the archive close.

runtime_observation.positive_control: Each case observed an intentionally open fixture handle and 0 after its explicit close.
limits: No evidence of retained fixture handles in these baseline loader cases.
The 4-to-306 warmup increase is a classpath-harness observation, not an IDE leak finding; individual warmup target differences were not serialized in this run.
No Windows locking experiment or full Eclipse/OSGi handle inventory was performed by this probe.
No timing benefit or absence of leaks in unrelated Eclipse plugins is established.

storage_stream_fix.change: Pass the existing try-with-resources stream to fSchema.load(stream), eliminating the second getContents() call.
storage_stream_fix.baseline: 3 tests started, 1 successful, 2 failed: expected one opening, observed two.
storage_stream_fix.closure_observation: Close assertions passed on the baseline too with this JDK/parser. A resource leak was not demonstrated.
